newsitem.title: INDIA: GOLD - INDIAN SUB-CONTINENT PRICES SEEN MIXED.
newsitem.headline: GOLD - INDIAN SUB-CONTINENT PRICES SEEN MIXED.

text.p: Subdued demand in India and rising jewellery exports in Pakistan may keep gold prices in the sub-continent mixed in the current week, dealers said on Monday.
Dealers said weekend tax raids on two well-known bullion traders in Bombay, India's main commercial city, had unnerved the market, burdened slightly with improved arrivals.
"Marketmen are a bit nervous, though there's no panic as such," said a dealer.
Standard gold slid 30 rupees to 4,500 rupees per 10 grammes on the Bombay bullion market in the week to Monday.
Dealers said the raids appeared to have been aimed at pushing tax-dodgers to take advantage of a voluntary scheme designed to unearth "black" or unaccounted money.
A week ago similar raids had been carried out on manufacturers of some popular brands of chewing tobacco.
"It appears the government is sending out a warning to those reluctant to disclose unaccounted wealth," the dealer said.
Dealers said they expected rural demand for gold to rise as crop prospects across the country had brightened with the four-month June-September monsoon rains satisfactory so far.
They said a Hindu festival season beginning later this month and lasting till October would keep bullion prices firm.
"I am expecting higher demand for gold," said another dealer. "But supplies may be affected for a few days because of the tax raids."
In Karachi, Pakistan's main business centre, gold prices are expected to rise in the current week on prospects of improved jewellery exports, dealers said.
"We see a slight rise in the demand for gold for jewellery and its export in the coming months," said dealer Saeed Qureshi of All Pakistan Gem and Jewellers' Association.
Dealers in Dubai said the rising demand for gold from the Indian sub-continent, had pushed up gold imports into the Gulf trading hub.
Dubai's gold imports had already surged to the record 1996 level in a rush, sparked by weak world prices, they said.
"Imports are surging because demand has been extremely high from major consuming markets, including India," said D.V. Pathy, a senior official of the World Gold Council (WGC).
India, the world's largest consumer of gold, is expected to import up to 500 tonnes in calendar 1997 against 409 tonnes in the previous year.
Dealers estimated gold imports into the United Arab Emirates at 350 tonnes till July-end, the same as imported in entire 1996.
"Prices have dropped this year and we have had good demand," said a dealer.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMMES in U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion $1=35.70 Indian rupees, 40.62 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE
Dirhams) *Bombay/Karachi prices Aug 11/4 and Dubai Aug 10/3.
